rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The wicked-versus-good distinction separates the people of felicity from the people of misery.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ليميز الله الخبيث من الطيب} فيميز أهل السعادة من أهل الشقاء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The distinction is between believer and unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: يميز المؤمن من الكافر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible distinction occurs in the Hereafter, separating associators from their partners and separating groups at resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهذا يحتمل أن يكون هذا التمييز في الآخرة، كما قال تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this distinction appears in worldly conduct, visible to believers, as obedience in fighting enemies versus disobediently hanging back.
rows.anchor: أي: من يطيعه بقتال أعدائه الكافرين، أو يعصيه بالنكول عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the worldly reading, the causal lām explains why God enables unbelievers to spend wealth obstructing the path: the ordeal distinguishes people.
rows.anchor: أي: إنما أقدرناهم على ذلك؛ {ليميز الله الخبيث من الطيب}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers the wicked together, piling them up as rakkama means collecting things upon one another, as with piled clouds; they are the losers in both worlds.
rows.anchor: {فيركمه} أي: يجمعه كله، وهو جمع الشيء بعضه على بعض

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb says he missed no expedition except Tabuk, apart from Badr, where absentees were not blamed; he valued the Aqaba pledge more than Badr despite Badr's greater fame.
rows.anchor: فقال كعب بن مالك: لم أتخلف عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Badr had been an unintended meeting: the Messenger set out for Quraysh's caravan, and God brought the two sides together without an appointment.
rows.anchor: ولم يعاتب أحد تخلف عنها، وإنما خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يريد عير قريش

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb was more able and prosperous than ever, having assembled two mounts for Tabuk, but the campaign came in severe heat across a distant, difficult route against many enemies.
rows.anchor: وكان من خبري حين تخلفت عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك أني لم أكن قط أقوى ولا أيسر مني

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet usually concealed a campaign's destination, but disclosed Tabuk so Muslims could prepare for its distant journey and numerous enemy; the large force had no roster.
rows.anchor: فجلى للمسلمين أمرهم ليتأهبوا أهبة عدوهم، فأخبرهم وجهه الذي يريد

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Though fruit and shade made the expedition appealing, Kaʿb repeatedly postponed preparations, expecting to catch up, until the army departed and he could not complete his equipment.
rows.anchor: وطفقت أغدو لكي أتجهز معهم

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: After the army left, Kaʿb regretted not pursuing it; among those remaining he saw only a suspected hypocrite or someone excused by God, and the Prophet did not ask about him until Tabuk.
rows.anchor: فهممت أن أرتحل فأدركهم

rows.speaker: رجل من بني سلمة
rows.claim: A man from Banu Salama blamed Kaʿb's clothes and vanity for his absence; Muʿadh rebuked him and testified that he knew only good of Kaʿb, while the Prophet stayed silent.
rows.anchor: قال رجل من بني سلمة: حبسه يا رسول الله برداه، والنظر في عطفيه. فقال له معاذ بن جبل: بئسما قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More than eighty absentees offered excuses and oaths; the Prophet accepted their outward professions, sought forgiveness for them, and left their inner realities to God.
rows.anchor: وكانوا بضعة وثمانين رجلا -فقبل منهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم علانيتهم ويستغفر لهم، ويكل سرائرهم إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: On hearing the Prophet was returning, Kaʿb considered lies but concluded he could not escape God's knowledge and resolved to tell the truth.
rows.anchor: زاح عني الباطل وعرفت أني لم أنج منه بشيء أبدا. فأجمعت صدقه

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb admits he had no excuse and was fully able to go; the Prophet confirms his truthfulness and tells him to wait for God's judgment.
rows.anchor: والله ما كان لي عذر، والله ما كنت قط أفرغ ولا أيسر مني حين تخلفت عنك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After Kaʿb tells the truth, the Prophet says he has spoken truly and orders him to wait until God decides his case.
rows.anchor: أما هذا فقد صدق، فقم حتى يقضي الله فيك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Some Banu Salama urged Kaʿb to make an excuse like the others; he nearly recanted, then learned that Murara and Hilal had also told the truth.
rows.anchor: قلت: فمن هما؟ قالوا: مرارة بن الربيع العامري، وهلال بن أمية الواقفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet prohibited Muslims from speaking to the three truthful absentees; the boycott lasted fifty nights, making even familiar earth seem strange to Kaʿb.
rows.anchor: حتى تنكرت لي في نفسي الأرض، فما هي بالأرض التي كنت أعرف

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Murara and Hilal stayed home crying, while Kaʿb kept attending prayer and markets; people ignored him, and the Prophet looked away when Kaʿb sought his gaze.
rows.anchor: فأما صاحباي فاستكانا وقعدا في بيوتهما يبكيان، وأما أنا فكنت أشب القوم وأجلدهم

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb asked his cousin Abu Qatada to affirm his love for God and the Messenger; Abu Qatada stayed silent, then replied that God and His Messenger knew best, and Kaʿb wept.
rows.anchor: فقلت له: يا أبا قتادة، أنشدك الله: هل تعلم أني أحب الله ورسوله؟ قال: فسكت

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: A Ghassan ruler's letter said the Prophet had abandoned Kaʿb and invited him to join; Kaʿb recognized this as another trial and burned it.
rows.anchor: أما بعد، فقد بلغنا أن صاحبك قد جفاك ولم يجعلك الله بدار هوان ولا مضيعة، فالحق بنا نواسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forty nights the Prophet ordered the three to separate from their wives; Hilal's wife was allowed to serve her helpless, grieving elderly husband but not approach him.
rows.anchor: فقالت له: يا رسول الله، إن هلالا شيخ ضائع ليس له خادم، فهل تكره أن أخدمه؟ قال: "لا ولكن لا يقربنك"

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb refused to seek permission to keep his wife, unsure what a young man would be told; after ten more nights, the three completed fifty nights of silence.
rows.anchor: فكمل لنا خمسون ليلة من حين نهى عن كلامنا

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: On the fiftieth morning, while Kaʿb felt the earth and his soul constrict, a caller on Mount Sala announced good news; he prostrated, recognizing that relief had come.
rows.anchor: سمعت صارخا أوفى على جبل سلع يقول بأعلى صوته: يا كعب بن مالك، أبشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: News of God's acceptance reached the Prophet at dawn; messengers hurried to the three, and the caller's voice outran a mounted messenger.
rows.anchor: فآذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بتوبة الله علينا حين صلى الفجر

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb gave the two garments he owned to the man who brought the news, then borrowed two garments and set out for the Messenger.
rows.anchor: والله ما أملك غيرهما يومئذ

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Talha alone among the Emigrants stood to congratulate Kaʿb, who never forgot it; the joyful Prophet called this the best day since Kaʿb's birth and said the good news came from God.
rows.anchor: فكان كعب لا ينساها لطلحة

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb offered to give all his wealth in charity, but the Prophet told him to retain some, so he kept his share at Khaybar; Kaʿb vowed to speak only truth thereafter.
rows.anchor: أمسك عليك بعض مالك، فهو خير لك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb regards his truthful confession as his greatest blessing after Islam and hopes God will preserve his truthfulness for life.
rows.anchor: فوالله ما أنعم الله علي من نعمة قط بعد أن هداني للإسلام أعظم في نفسي من صدقي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يومئذ

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: God revealed the account of the three and the command to be with the truthful; Kaʿb contrasts their truthful confession with those who lied and were condemned.
rows.anchor: وأنزل الله تعالى: {لقد تاب الله على النبي والمهاجرين والأنصار الذين اتبعوه في ساعة العسرة

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet accepted the oath-taking absentees and sought forgiveness for them but postponed the three truthful men's case; khalafu here means deferred, not merely staying behind from battle.
rows.anchor: فبذلك قال الله تعالى: (23) {وعلى الثلاثة الذين خلفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of the three is sound and agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim; Ibn Kathir says it gives the verse's clearest and fullest interpretation.
rows.anchor: هذا حديث صحيح ثابت متفق على صحته، رواه صاحبا الصحيح: البخاري ومسلم من حديث الزهري

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir identifies the three as Kaʿb ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murara ibn Rabiʿa, all from the Ansar.
rows.anchor: قال: هم كعب بن مالك، وهلال بن أمية، ومرارة بن ربيعة وكلهم من الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatada, al-Suddi, and others identify Murara; reports vary between forms of his name, but Ibn Kathir prefers Murara ibn al-Rabiʿa, matching the two Sahih collections.
rows.anchor: كما وقع في الصحيحين، وهو الصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that two of the three had fought at Badr is probably a mistake by al-Zuhri, since none of the three is known to have attended Badr.
rows.anchor: قيل: إنه خطأ من الزهري، فإنه لا يعرف شهود واحد من هؤلاء الثلاثة بدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslim estrangement closed every route for the three for nearly fifty days; they endured patiently and were finally relieved because they truthfully admitted having no excuse.
rows.anchor: وضاقت عليهم أنفسهم، وضاقت عليهم الأرض بما رحبت، أي: مع سعتها، فسددت عليهم المسالك والمذاهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to tell the truth and remain with truthful people, gaining safety from peril and relief from difficult affairs.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وكونوا مع الصادقين} أي: اصدقوا والزموا الصدق تكونوا مع أهله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet teaches that persistent truth leads to righteousness and Paradise and earns the truthful person the designation siddiq, while persistent lying leads to wickedness, Hell, and the designation liar.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "عليكم بالصدق؛ فإن الصدق يهدي إلى البر وإن البر يهدي إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding report about truth is also transmitted in both Sahih collections.
rows.anchor: أخرجاه في الصحيحين. (1) وقال شعبة، عن عمرو بن مرة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says lying is wrong in earnest or jest, recites the phrase with min al-sadiqin, and asks whether anyone can find a license for it.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، أنه قال: [إن] (2) الكذب لا يصلح منه جد ولا هزل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar interprets being with the truthful as being with Muhammad and his Companions.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمر: {اتقوا الله وكونوا مع الصادقين} مع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the truthful company as Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, and their Companions.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: مع أبي بكر وعمر وأصحابهما

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan says joining the truthful requires renouncing worldly attachment and refraining from harming the people of the faith.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: إن أردت أن تكون مع الصادقين، فعليك بالزهد في الدنيا، والكف عن أهل الملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain-grown crops and fruits for people and pasture for animals portray worldly life's beauty, brief flourishing, and swift disappearance.
rows.anchor: تعالى مثلا لزهرة الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وسرعة انقضائها وزوالها، بالنبات الذي أخرجه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth takes its fading ornament, blooms in varied forms and colors, and its owners expect to harvest; then a sudden command by night or day leaves it dry and destroyed, as if never beautiful.
rows.anchor: أتاها أمرنا ليلا أو نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains the phrase about the land seeming never to have flourished as meaning it had never enjoyed prosperity.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: {كأن لم تغن} كأن لم تنعم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly affairs after their disappearance seem never to have existed; a person given the greatest worldly bliss forgets it after one dip in Hell, and the most miserable forgets suffering after one dip in delight.
rows.anchor: يؤتى بأنعم أهل الدنيا، فيغمس في النار غمسة ثم يقال له: هل رأيت خيرا قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable urges reflection on the world's rapid passing despite people's confidence; God also compares worldly life to vegetation elsewhere.
rows.anchor: فيعتبرون بهذا المثل في زوال الدنيا من أهلها سريعا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Ubayy ibn Kaʿb taught a reading adding that God would not destroy the land except for its people's sins; Ibn Kathir calls it unusual and likely an explanatory addition.
rows.anchor: هكذا أقرأني أبي بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the world's rapid decay, God invites people to Paradise, called the Abode of Peace because it is free of afflictions, defects, and calamities, and guides whom He wills straight.
rows.anchor: أي: من الآفات، والنقائص والنكبات

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a mursal parable, God is the master, Islam the house, Paradise the banquet, and Muhammad the caller; those who answer enter and are welcomed, while those who refuse miss all three.
rows.anchor: فالله السيد، والدار الإسلام، والمأدبة الجنة، والداعي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A connected Jabir version pictures a king's house and banquet: the house is Islam, its inner house is Paradise, and whoever answers Muhammad enters Islam and then Paradise.
rows.anchor: فالله الملك، والدار الإسلام، والبيت الجنة، وأنت يا محمد الرسول

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that two angels beside the sun call all creatures except humans and jinn to their Lord, declaring that a little sufficient provision is better than abundant distraction; Qatada says this was revealed in the verse.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الناس، هلموا إلى ربكم، إن ما قل وكفى، خير مما كثر وألهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection, people gathered from their graves will feel that they lived in this world only a brief part of a day; this demonstrates the world's brevity relative to the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: كأنهم (7) يوم يوافونها لم يلبثوا في الدنيا {إلا ساعة من النهار}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will recognize children, parents, and relatives as in worldly life, though each will be preoccupied; kinship will not prompt mutual concern.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {يتعارفون بينهم} أي: يعرف الأبناء الآباء (8) والقرابات بعضهم لبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who denied meeting God lose themselves and their families through separation from beloved ones on the Day of Regret, the greatest loss.
rows.anchor: ولا خسارة أعظم من خسارة من فرق بينه وبين أحبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers' demand to know when punishment will come is useless; believers know the Hour is certain even if its exact time is unknown.
rows.anchor: استعجالهم العذاب وسؤالهم عن وقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger controls neither harm nor benefit except by God's will, speaks only what God teaches, and was told the Hour would occur but not when.
rows.anchor: أي: لا أقول إلا ما علمني، ولا أقدر على شيء مما استأثر به إلا أن يطلعني عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every community has a measured term; when it arrives, no delay or advancement is possible.
rows.anchor: فإذا انقضى أجلهم {فلا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment may arrive unexpectedly by night or day; criminals will believe only when it comes, like peoples whose professions of faith after seeing punishment brought no benefit.
rows.anchor: يعني: أنهم إذا جاءهم العذاب قالوا: {ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel left Egypt with Moses; some reports count six hundred thousand fighters besides children and say they carried Egyptian jewelry, enraging Pharaoh, who mustered his entire realm's forces.
rows.anchor: وهم -فيما قيل -ستمائة ألف مقاتل سوى الذرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh caught Israel at sunrise by the sea; although they feared capture, Moses trusted God's guidance, struck the sea, and God opened twelve routes, one for each tribe, dried by wind with watery windows between.
rows.anchor: أي: كالجبل العظيم، وصار اثني عشر طريقا، لكل سبط واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's force reached the far shore with a hundred thousand dark horses and other colors; Gabriel's horse drew Pharaoh's stallion into the sea, while Michael drove the army from behind.
rows.anchor: وهو في مائة ألف أدهم سوى بقية الألوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the entire army entered and began to emerge, God ordered the sea to crash over them; no one escaped, and waves piled over Pharaoh as he drowned.
rows.anchor: أمر الله القدير البحر أن يرتطم عليهم، فارتطم عليهم، فلم ينج منهم أحد

rows.speaker: فرعون
rows.claim: At death Pharaoh professed faith in Israel's God, but faith after punishment began was useless, as with earlier punished unbelievers.
rows.anchor: فآمن حيث لا ينفعه الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reply means Pharaoh professes faith only now, after prior disobedience; he had corrupted the earth by misleading people.
rows.anchor: أي: أهذا (2) الوقت تقول، وقد عصيت الله قبل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's exact words at death are among hidden matters God disclosed to His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي حكى الله تعالى عن فرعون

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet saying Gabriel took mud from the sea and put it in Pharaoh's mouth, fearing that mercy would reach him; al-Tirmidhi grades this route hasan.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لما قال فرعون: {آمنت أنه لا إله إلا الذي آمنت به بنو إسرائيل} قال: قال لي جبريل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second Ibn ʿAbbas route has al-Tirmidhi grading the report hasan gharib sahih; a Jarir route raises it through one of two narrators, while Ibn Kathir leaves that variation uncertain.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد، عن ابن عباس، رفعه أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir also transmits the Abu Khalid report from Ibn ʿAbbas as mawquf rather than attributing it to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وكذا رواه ابن جرير، عن سفيان بن وكيع، عن أبي خالد، به موقوفا (7)

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying Gabriel gagged Pharaoh with sea mud lest God's mercy reach him; the narrator Kathir ibn Zadhan is unknown to Ibn Maʿin, Abu Zurʿa, and Abu Hatim, though the rest are reliable.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "قال لي جبريل: يا محمد، لو رأيتني وأنا أغطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report is also sent as a mursal narration from Qatada, Ibrahim al-Taymi, and Maymun ibn Mihran; it was preached by al-Dahhak ibn Qays, and Ibn Kathir says God knows best.
rows.anchor: وقد أرسل هذا الحديث جماعة من السلف: قتادة، وإبراهيم التيمي، وميمون بن مهران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should reflect on God's signs in the heavens: fixed and moving stars, sun and moon, alternating day and night, and the sky's height, breadth, beauty, and adornment.
rows.anchor: من كواكب نيرات، ثوابت وسيارات، والشمس والقمر، والليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth's rain revives it with fruits, crops, flowers, and varied plants; it holds diverse animals, mountains, plains, wilderness, settlements, and ruins.
rows.anchor: وما أنزل الله منها من مطر فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea's wonders and waves are nevertheless subdued for travelers, carrying ships gently by God's power; He alone is God and Lord.
rows.anchor: مذلل للسالكين، يحمل سفنهم، ويجري بها برفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither heavenly or earthly signs nor messengers' proofs benefit people destined not to believe; they persist until they see painful punishment.
rows.anchor: إن الذين حقت عليهم كلمة ربك لا يؤمنون ولو جاءتهم كل آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers await punishment like earlier nations; God destroys the deniers and saves His messengers and believers, a deliverance He has made binding upon Himself.
rows.anchor: {قل فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين ثم ننجي رسلنا والذين آمنوا}

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith in both Sahih collections says God wrote that His mercy precedes His anger.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "إن الله كتب كتابا فهو عنده فوق العرش: إن رحمتي سبقت (7) غضبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says ostentatious people receive in this world the reward for good deeds done solely for worldly gain, such as fasting, prayer, or night vigil, but their work is void in the Hereafter; Mujahid and al-Dahhak also report this view.
rows.anchor: إن أهل الرياء يعطون بحسناتهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas and Hasan say these verses were revealed about Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: وقال أنس بن مالك، والحسن: نزلت في اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and others identify the people addressed as those who act for show.
rows.anchor: وهكذا روي عن مجاهد، والضحاك، وغير واحد.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says those whose goal and intention are worldly receive their good deeds' reward here, then arrive with no rewarded good deed; believers are rewarded both here and in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: من كانت الدنيا همه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's fourth son, named Yam, was an unbeliever; Noah urged him to board with the believers, but he trusted a mountain to shield him from the flood.
rows.anchor: هذا هو الابن الرابع، واسمه "يام"، وكان كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A claim that the son built a glass boat is an Israelite report whose reliability Ibn Kathir does not know; the Qur'an says only that he sought a mountain.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه اتخذ له مركبا من زجاج، وهذا من الإسرائيليات، والله أعلم بصحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son ignorantly believed the flood would not reach mountain peaks; Noah said no one could protect himself from God's decree except one shown mercy, with an alternative reading of asim as protected.
rows.anchor: اعتقد بجهله أن الطوفان لا يبلغ إلى رءوس الجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative takes asim as maʿsum, like words meaning something eaten or worn; the wave separated father and son, and the son drowned.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن عاصما بمعنى معصوم، كما يقال: "طاعم وكاس"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the Messenger and believers to persist in the prescribed straight path; steadfastness is a major aid to victory over enemies and opponents.
rows.anchor: يأمر تعالى رسوله وعباده المؤمنين بالثبات والدوام على الاستقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must not transgress: oppression is ruinous even when directed against polytheists, and God sees every deed.
rows.anchor: ونهى عن الطغيان، وهو البغي، فإنه مصرعة حتى ولو كان على مشرك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains not leaning toward wrongdoers as not being complaisant with them; another report from him interprets it as leaning toward associationism.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: لا تدهنوا

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya interprets the warning as not approving wrongdoers' deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: لا ترضوا أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj's report from Ibn ʿAbbas says not to incline toward oppressors; Ibn Kathir approves it and explains that this includes not seeking their help, lest one seem to approve their conduct and incur Hell.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول حسن، أي: لا تستعينوا بالظلمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Hasan, and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd identify the two ends of day as morning and sunset prayers.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} قال: يعني الصبح والمغرب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan in another report, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others identify the prayers as dawn and afternoon.
rows.anchor: هي الصبح والعصر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, and al-Dahhak in another report identify them as dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هي الصبح في أول النهار، والظهر والعصر من آخره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Hasan, and others take the night approaches to mean the night prayer.
rows.anchor: يعني صلاة العشاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan in another report, along with Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, Qatada, and al-Dahhak, identifies them as sunset and night prayers; a prophetic report calls these the night's two approaches.
rows.anchor: هما زلفتا (1) الليل: المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may predate the five daily prayers prescribed on the Night Journey: initially two daily prayers and night vigil were required, then night vigil was abrogated for the community, remained for the Prophet, and, in one view, was later abrogated for him too.
rows.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن تكون هذه الآية نزلت قبل فرض الصلوات الخمس ليلة الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good deeds erase earlier sins, as shown by reports that a sinner who performs ablution and prays two units is forgiven.
rows.anchor: إن فعل الخيرات يكفر الذنوب السالفة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: The Prophet says a Muslim who sins, performs ablution, and prays two rakʿas is forgiven; Abu Bakr affirmed that he heard this from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "ما من مسلم يذنب ذنبا، فيتوضأ ويصلي ركعتين، إلا غفر له

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: In the two Sahih collections, Uthman demonstrates the Prophet's ablution and says that performing it and praying two units without distracting thoughts forgives prior sins.
rows.anchor: وقال: "من توضأ نحو وضوئي هذا، ثم صلى ركعتين لا يحدث فيهما نفسه، غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: Another report from Uthman says each prayer forgives sins committed since the previous prayer, and ablution and dawn prayer forgive the night; these are good deeds that erase sins.
rows.anchor: وهن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet compares five daily prayers to bathing five times in a river at one's door: just as dirt would not remain, the prayers erase sins.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الصلوات الخمس، يمحو الله بهن الذنوب والخطايا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The five prayers, one Friday to the next, and one Ramadan to the next expiate sins between them when major sins are avoided.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: "الصلوات الخمس، والجمعة إلى الجمعة، ورمضان إلى رمضان، مكفرات ما بينهن إذا (3) اجتنبت الكبائر"

rows.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
rows.claim: The Prophet says each prayer removes the sins that preceded it.
rows.anchor: إن كل صلاة تحط ما بين يديها من خطيئة

rows.speaker: أبو مالك الأشعري
rows.claim: The Prophet says prayers were made expiations for what lies between them, citing the verse that good deeds remove evil deeds.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مالك الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "جعلت الصلوات كفارات لما بينهن؛ فإن الله قال

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In one account a man confesses kissing a woman; the Prophet recites the verse and says its promise applies to all his community.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود؛ أن رجلا أصاب من امرأة قبلة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In another account the man describes kissing and embracing a woman without intercourse; after the Prophet recalls him and recites the verse, ʿUmar or Muʿadh asks whether it is only for him, and the Prophet says it is for everyone.
rows.anchor: جاء رجل إلى النبي (1) صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says God distributes character as He distributes provision: He grants worldly life to those He loves and those He does not, but grants faith only to those He loves; faith requires a surrendered heart and tongue and a neighbor safe from harm.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله قسم بينكم أخلاقكم (3) كما قسم بينكم أرزاقكم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The same report says illicit wealth is not blessed or accepted as charity and becomes provision for Hell; God erases evil with good, since evil cannot erase evil.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يمحو السيئ بالسيئ، ولكنه يمحو السيئ بالحسن

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim reports an unnamed Ansari who had sexual contact with a woman short of intercourse; the Prophet could not answer until this verse was revealed, then recited it to him.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: كان فلان ابن معتب رجلا من الأنصار، فقال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Reports differ over the man's identity: Ibn ʿAbbas names ʿAmr ibn Ghaziya al-Ansari al-Tammar; Muqatil says Abu Nufayl ʿAmir ibn Qays; al-Khatib says Abu al-Yusr Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أنه عمرو بن غزية الأنصاري التمار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A man who had done less than intercourse with a woman brought his case first to ʿUmar and Abu Bakr, then the Prophet; after the verse came, ʿUmar said its remedy was for everyone, and the Prophet affirmed him.
rows.anchor: بل للناس عامة. فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "صدق عمر"

rows.speaker: أبو اليسر كعب بن عمرو الأنصاري
rows.claim: A woman came to buy dates; Abu al-Yusr invited her inside and kissed her, then confessed to ʿUmar, Abu Bakr, and the Prophet, who reproached him for betraying a man away fighting; Gabriel brought the verse, which applies to all.
rows.anchor: أتتني امرأة تبتاع مني بدرهم تمرا

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: A man who touched an unlawful woman in every way short of intercourse was told by the Prophet to make a careful ablution and pray; the verse came, and the Prophet said it applied to all Muslims.
rows.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "توضأ وضوءا حسنا، ثم قم فصل"

rows.speaker: يحيى بن جعدة
rows.claim: A mursal report tells of a Companion who found a woman at a pool, touched her short of intercourse, regretted it, and confessed; the Prophet told him to seek forgiveness and pray four units, then recited the verse.
rows.anchor: فأخبره بما صنع، فقال له: "استغفر ربك، وصل أربع ركعات"

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: A man asking to receive God's prescribed penalty was ignored until after prayer; the Prophet asked whether he had performed ablution and prayed with them, then said he was cleansed like a newborn and must not repeat the sin.
rows.anchor: فإنك من خطيئتك كما ولدتك أمك، ولا تعد

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
rows.claim: The Prophet shook a dry branch so its leaves fell and likened this to a Muslim whose careful ablution and five prayers shed sins; he recited the verse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عثمان قال: كنت مع سلمان الفارسي تحت شجرة، فأخذ منها غصنا يابسا

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Muʿadh to follow a bad deed with a good one that erases it, and to treat people with good character.
rows.anchor: عن معاذ، رضي الله عنه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له: "يا معاذ، أتبع السيئة الحسنة تمحها

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: The Prophet gives Abu Dharr the same counsel: fear God everywhere, follow a bad deed with a good one, and treat people well.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أحمد، رضي الله عنه: حدثنا وكيع، حدثنا سفيان، عن حبيب، عن ميمون بن أبي شبيب، عن أبي ذر

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: The Prophet advises Abu Dharr to follow every sin with a good deed to erase it and says that proclaiming there is no god but God is the best of good deeds.
rows.anchor: هي أفضل الحسنات

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: A report says whoever says there is no god but God at any hour has the sins in the record erased until good deeds balance them; Ibn Kathir notes that Uthman al-Waqqasi is weak.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما قال عبد: لا إله إلا الله، في ساعة من ليل

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A man says he has left no need or small matter undone; the Prophet asks whether he testifies that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His Messenger, and says this testimony covers it all; this route is unique through Mastur.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "تشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأني رسول الله؟

rows.speaker: يوسف
rows.claim: Joseph prefers prison to the indecency they invite him to; recognizing his dependence on God, he asks to be turned from their plot rather than left to his own weakness.
rows.anchor: السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Joseph, turned the women's plot away, and protected him; Joseph chose prison over sin despite youth, beauty, and a powerful, beautiful woman inviting him, seeking God's fear and reward.
rows.anchor: ويختار السجن على ذلك، خوفا من الله ورجاء ثوابه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in both Sahih collections says seven types receive God's shade, including a young person raised in worship and a man invited by a beautiful, high-status woman who replies that he fears God.
rows.anchor: ورجل دعته امرأة ذات جمال ومنصب، فقال: إني أخاف الله
